headline: Saudi attacks lift Brent 4% to $113 as an AI-led flight to safety pulls the 10-year below 5%
summary: Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia and reports of renewed US strikes on Iran sent Brent up $4.35 to $113.17, its highest settle in over five months, with December WTI up 2.4% at $99.47 and RBOB up 1.8% to $3.1765. Metals ignored the bond rally: gold fell nearly 3% to about $4,025, its lowest since early August, and silver dropped close to 6%. An AI-stock selloff and French turmoil drove the biggest one-day fall in the US 10-year yield since March 2023, to 4.95%, while Bunds rallied and France's spread to Germany hit about 175bp, the widest since 2011.
drivers: A Houthi drone hit Saudi Aramco's Shaybah field, killing two though output was unaffected, the US ordered some diplomats out of Saudi Arabia, and a report said the US and Israel plan renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms. Brent rose 4% to $113.17 and WTI touched $100.17 before settling at $99.47.

A slide in AI stocks after disappointing earnings, plus French stress, drove a broad bond rally: at the 3pm close the 10-year fell 19bp to 4.952% and the 2-year 19bp to 4.635%. Jobless claims of 194,000, below the 200,000 forecast, and a solid $26B 5-year TIPS sale did not stop it; October hike odds fell to about 7%.

The 10-year OAT touched 5.142%, the highest since 2002, and closed near 5.08% while the Bund fell about 8bp to 3.34%, taking the spread to roughly 175bp, the widest since November 2011. Belgian and Italian spreads also widened about 10bp ahead of Friday's Moody's review.

Gold broke the $4,070 floor of its October range as oil revived inflation and December-hike fears (still priced near 85–90%) and as investors raised cash; December futures fell $89.60 to about $4,060. Silver lost close to 6% to about $54.6 on industrial-demand worries.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled up $2.32 (+2.4%) at $99.47 after a $100.17 high; Brent up $4.35 (+4%) at $113.17.
oil.why: Crude jumped as the Gulf war widened: a Houthi drone struck Aramco's Shaybah field, killing two, Dammam's airport was attacked and Yanbu port was targeted, and the US told some diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia. A report that the US and Israel plan new strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms, and Trump saying there are no talks with Tehran, added risk premium. Brent outran WTI, stretching the spread to about $13.70.
oil.outlook: Bias higher while attacks continue: Brent $108–118 and WTI $95–104. Hormuz crude flows back near pre-war levels cap the upside; a Brent close above $115 targets the $118 March peak, and a US–Iran opening would knock it back toward $105.
oil.watch: Saudi infrastructure attacks, Hormuz tanker strikes, EIA data Oct 28 and OPEC+ on Nov 1.

gas.note: Nov RBOB rose 5.60¢ (+1.8%) to $3.1765 after a $3.2205 high; AAA pump average about $4.27.
gas.why: Gasoline followed crude higher on the Saudi attacks, posting its biggest gain since Oct 8, and drew support from Wednesday's EIA data showing stocks 5% below the five-year average after a 3.0M-barrel draw. Diesel rose more, up about 17¢ to $4.93, as Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries tightened product markets. Pump prices are still falling, down about 6¢ in a week, on the cheaper winter blend.
gas.outlook: Range $3.05–3.30, with crude in the driving seat. Low stocks support it, but seasonal demand and the winter-blend switch limit upside; a close above $3.25 would need Brent beyond $115.
gas.watch: Nov RBOB expiry Oct 30, EIA data Oct 28 and the AAA weekly average.

gold.note: Spot about $4,025, down nearly 3%, the lowest since early August; Dec futures down $89.60 near $4,060.
gold.why: Gold fell for a fifth day and broke the $4,070 floor that had held all month, as oil's spike revived inflation worries and kept a December Fed hike priced near 85–90%. It did not benefit from the 19bp drop in Treasury yields: investors sold bullion to raise cash during the equity slide, and stop-loss selling accelerated once support gave way. Mining shares fell more than 5%.
gold.outlook: Bias lower with a $3,950–4,140 range into the Fed. Holding $4,000 matters; below it, chart targets near $3,915 come into view. A close back above $4,080 would signal a false break.
gold.watch: Oil and Gulf headlines, Friday's PMIs and the Fed decision on Oct 28.

silver.note: Spot about $54.6, down close to 6%; gold/silver ratio near 74.
silver.why: Silver fell about twice as hard as gold as the tech-led equity slide and growth worries hit industrial metals, with copper also down more than 2%. Oil-driven rate-hike fears and liquidation in precious metals added to the pressure, taking it below the $56.30 support and through the $54.75 level Kitco had flagged.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $52.50–57.00 range. It needs a close back above $56.30 to stabilise; risk appetite and copper set the tone more than gold.
silver.watch: Equity sentiment, China data, the dollar and the Fed on Oct 28.

us2y.note: Fell about 19bp to 4.635% at the 3pm close, its biggest one-day drop since August 2025.
us2y.why: The 2-year plunged as an AI-led stock selloff and French stress sparked a flight to safety and traders cut the odds of an October hike to about 7%, from 28% a week ago. Jobless claims of 194,000, below the 200,000 forecast, briefly pared the rally. December is still priced for a hike at roughly 85–90%, which limits how far the front end can fall.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.55–4.80% until the Fed. A hawkish signal for December would pull it back toward 4.75%; continued equity stress or a soft statement opens 4.55%.
us2y.watch: The Fed on Oct 27–28, October jobs data and equity markets.

us5y.note: About 4.78%, down roughly 19bp; the belly led the rally.
us5y.why: The 5-year fell most on the curve as investors bought intermediate notes for safety during the equity slide and priced a shorter hiking cycle. A solid $26B 5-year TIPS auction, with 94.5% taken by non-dealers against a 90.8% average, added support, while the 5-year breakeven slipped to about 2.38% from 2.41%.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.70–4.95%. Oil above $110 keeps inflation risk alive, so a Fed that stresses more hikes would push it back toward 4.90%.
us5y.watch: Friday's PMIs, the Fed on Oct 28 and the 2-, 5- and 7-year auctions.

us10y.note: Down 19.3bp to 4.952% at the 3pm close (Tradeweb), the biggest drop since March 2023 and lowest since Sept 17.
us10y.why: The 10-year fell below 5% for the first time in a month as AI stocks slid on disappointing earnings and worries about debt-funded AI spending, and as French turmoil drew money into safe bonds. Concern that $110 oil will hurt consumer spending outweighed its inflation effect for the day. Mortgage rates fell for the first time in nine weeks.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.85–5.10%. Oil near $100 and heavy supply limit the downside; a hawkish Fed would likely push it back above 5%, while a deeper equity selloff could test 4.85%.
us10y.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, oil, AI-sector earnings and the Nov 4 refunding.

us30y.note: Down 15.1bp to 5.286%, its biggest daily fall since August 2024; the curve steepened slightly.
us30y.why: The long bond rallied with the rest of the curve on haven demand but less than shorter notes, so the 2s–30s curve steepened. Supply and term-premium worries, with the midterms on Nov 3 and the refunding on Nov 4, kept investors cautious about the longest maturities even as yields fell.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.20–5.40%. The refunding decides the next move: smaller long-bond sizes would extend the rally, unchanged sizes would push term premium back up.
us30y.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, the midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.

de2y.note: Down about 6bp to near 3.02%, tracking the Treasury rally.
de2y.why: The Schatz rallied as risk-off flows and French stress drew money into German debt, despite oil above $110. Money markets still price the ECB deposit rate near 3.15% by end-2027, two more quarter-point hikes and a good chance of a third, but no move at next week's meeting.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.95–3.10%. A hawkish ECB on Oct 29 would lift it back toward 3.10%; deeper risk-off or a fall in oil would test 2.95%.
de2y.watch: Friday's flash PMIs, the ECB on Oct 29 and flash October inflation.

de5y.note: About 3.12%, down roughly 7–9bp with the rest of the Bund curve.
de5y.why: The 5-year Bund fell in line with the 2- and 10-year as investors swapped French and riskier euro-area bonds for German debt. Belgian, Italian and Spanish spreads all widened 6–10bp, a sign that the selling of French paper is spreading and pushing haven demand into Germany.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.05–3.20%. Continued French stress keeps it supported; a hawkish ECB or a rebound in risk appetite would lift it.
de5y.watch: Moody's on France Friday, the ECB on Oct 29 and the OAT–Bund spread.

de10y.note: Closed near 3.34%, down about 8bp; OAT–Bund spread about 175bp.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund had its biggest fall in weeks as a haven, with Dow Jones putting the close at 3.337%, down 7.9bp. The French selloff, global equity weakness and the plunge in Treasury yields outweighed oil's 4% jump. Analysts noted that German debt is again acting as the safe asset, pushing the spread to France to its widest since 2011.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.25–3.45%. French stress and risk-off cap it; a move back above 3.45% would need a hawkish ECB or a sharp recovery in equities.
de10y.watch: Moody's on France Friday, flash PMIs and the ECB on Oct 29.

de30y.note: About 3.68%, lower by roughly 6–9bp, tracking US long bonds.
de30y.why: The 30-year Bund rallied with US long bonds and haven demand, though it gained less than shorter maturities as supply concerns linger at the long end. Its move mirrored the 15bp drop in the US 30-year more than any change in the ECB outlook.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.80%. It follows US long bonds and global term premium more than the ECB.
de30y.watch: US long-end yields, the Nov 4 refunding and German long-dated sales.

fr2y.note: About 3.76%, little changed while the Schatz rallied; the 2-year spread to Germany widened to about 75bp.
fr2y.why: Short French paper did not join the German rally as political risk crept further into front-end pricing. With the 2027 budget stalled, more protests planned for Saturday and troops to be deployed alongside police, investors demanded more to hold even short-dated French debt, widening the gap to the Schatz by about 6bp.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.68–3.85%; it would jump only if a censure motion threatened the government or the budget collapsed.
fr2y.watch: Moody's Friday, protests Oct 24, the budget debate from Oct 27 and the ECB on Oct 29.

fr5y.note: About 4.45%, a little higher while Bunds rallied; the spread over Germany widened further.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT underperformed as the budget standoff and street protests kept pressure on French debt ahead of Friday's Moody's review, where most economists expect a downgrade from Aa3 to A1. With the deficit near 5% of GDP and debt heading toward 122% next year, investors are pricing more risk across the curve.
fr5y.outlook: Bias higher in a 4.35–4.60% range until the budget clears. A downgrade with a stable outlook may already be priced; a negative outlook would add pressure.
fr5y.watch: Moody's Friday Oct 23, Saturday's protests and the budget debate from Oct 27.

fr10y.note: Touched 5.142%, highest since 2002, and closed near 5.08%, up about 7–8bp; spread near 175bp.
fr10y.why: French 10-year yields rose even as Bunds and Treasuries rallied, pushing the OAT–Bund spread to about 174–178bp intraday, the widest since November 2011. Doubts that a fractured parliament will pass the 2027 budget, more protests planned for Saturday and an expected Moody's downgrade drove the selling. Belgian and Italian spreads widened about 10bp, showing early contagion.
fr10y.outlook: Spread bias wider in a 165–190bp range. Analysts say spreads are still far from the 200–250bp levels that prompted ECB action; a calm weekend and budget progress could pull it back toward 165bp.
fr10y.watch: Moody's Friday Oct 23, protests Oct 24, the budget debate from Oct 27 and the ECB on Oct 29.

fr30y.note: About 5.55%, holding near cycle highs while German long bonds rallied.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT stayed near its highs while the German 30-year fell sharply, as investors demanded a larger fiscal premium to hold long French debt through the budget fight and the 2027 presidential race. Debt-service costs above €90 billion and the risk of a downgrade weigh most on the long end.
fr30y.outlook: The most exposed part of the curve. A close above 5.60% would set a new cycle high; only a credible budget deal is likely to turn it.
fr30y.watch: Moody's Friday, the budget debate and long-dated OAT auctions.

watch: Next: Moody's on France and flash PMIs Friday, French protests Saturday, the budget debate from Oct 27, the Fed on Oct 28, EIA data Oct 28, the ECB on Oct 29, Nov RBOB expiry Oct 30, OPEC+ on Nov 1, the US midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.
sources: Dow Jones via MarketScreener (Treasuries, Bunds, OATs)
